Carlos — thanks for the clear list. Below is a short, worked commercial appendix response plus mechanics. I kept the math conservative and included two optional concessions that require finance approval.

Summary (top-line)
- Published token list price (hosted): $0.0038 per 1K prompt+completion tokens.
- Commit tiers (annualized): 100M tokens @ 15% discount, 300M @ 28% discount, 1B @ 38% discount off list. Effective per-1K prices (post-discount):
  - 100M commit: $0.00323 per 1K
  - 300M commit: $0.002736 per 1K
  - 1B commit: $0.002356 per 1K
- Overage / burst pricing: overage billed at list price for the month, with two smoothing options (auto-trueup or surge-deferral credit) described below.
- Pilot credit: up to $100k applied to year-1 invoice as a prepayment credit if customer converts to an annual commit within 60 days of pilot end.

Worked example (quarterly view)
Assumptions: 300M annual commit (25M tokens/month average), per-1K effective $0.002736.
Month A: 20M consumed (under by 5M)
Month B: 50M consumed (over by 25M)
Month C: 25M consumed (on target)
Quarter total consumption = 95M vs committed quarter volume (75M) -> quarter overage = 20M

Billing mechanics (default auto-trueup)
- Monthly invoices show list-price charges for actual consumption.
- Quarterly true-up applies the commit discount against total quarter consumption up to committed amount; any consumption above the committed quarter volume billed as overage at the overage rate (see options).
- Example charges (simplified):
  - List price charge for quarter actual = 95M * list unit equivalent (converted to 1K units)
  - Commit discount credit applied: 75M * discount differential -> net reduces invoice
  - Remaining 20M billed as overage at overage structure below.

Overage / surge handling (two options)
1) Standard overage: bill at list price for excess tokens. True-up annually; monthly/quarterly invoice shows overage charges. No smoothing.
2) Surge-deferral (optional concession): for a one-time per-year surge where any month exceeds 3x the monthly baseline AND total quarterly overage is less than 15% of committed quarter, customer may elect to defer up to 50% of that month’s overage into the next quarter as a one-time credit. Deferred amount converts to a negative invoice item applied against next quarter’s invoice and will be reconciled at annual true-up. This concession requires a 12-month commit and is limited to two occurrences in the contract term.

Optional credit ladder (approved by finance):
- If customer signs 24-month commitment, add an additional 3% ladder discount on top of the tiered discount for year-2 consumption above commit up to 20%.
- Pilot conversion: $100k pilot credit converts into committed volume credit at the committed tier rate; if customer declines conversion within 60 days, credit forfeited.

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Appendix_v3.pdf (detailed tier table, seat equivalency table, sample invoice flows).

Next steps:
1) If Delta prefers the Surge-deferral concession, confirm (a) target commit bucket and (b) limits (we recommend 300M minimum). Finance will need to approve and we’ll reflect in the commercial appendix.
2) We can provide a redline-ready pricing appendix for signature and a sample DocuSign.

Best,
Vivek
VP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
